criteria.justification: The response explicitly reframes the issue as 'no longer about finding the right words; it is a governance and decision-making failure,' addressing the repeated failure pattern rather than just this round's word choice.

It proposes a concrete rubric-and-meeting mechanism to force a decision, with an executive escalation fallback if consensus fails, and frames continued churn as burning cycles/delaying launch rather than being free.

It notes reviewers were 'free to veto a name the moment they spot a flaw' and assumes objections arose in silos with unweighed subjective criteria, but it never actually assesses whether each of the three prior objections was legitimate/new versus re-litigation—it treats them all as inputs to be weighed equally in a rubric rather than diagnosing diminishing returns explicitly.

The locked API name is treated as a fixed constraint throughout (listed in evidence, factored into the one-pager, and even evaluated as its own alternative before being set aside), and the recommendation is built around it rather than reopening it.

The recommendation explicitly says to 'Stop pitching names' and instead reset the process by aligning on a rubric first, directly distinguishing this approach from the three prior ad hoc name-picking attempts.
